title: Encapsulation
points: Keep fields private and let them change only through authorized methods.
The object controls its own state, so those methods can validate and protect invariants.
Returning a mutable internal collection lets callers bypass your rules. Return an unmodifiable view or a copy.
trade: A getter and setter on every private field is not real encapsulation. Expose behaviour (withdraw), not raw state. View vs copy: a view is cheap but changes with the original; a copy is a stable snapshot. Both are shallow.
test: Why does a private final List field with a getItems() that returns it still break encapsulation?
answer: Callers get the real list and can clear or modify it, bypassing your rules. Return an unmodifiable view or a copy, and change state only through methods that enforce the rules.
